subject: ventures/uk-working-from-home-tax-relief-calculator
professional: a UK chartered tax adviser (CTA) who files employee expense (P87) and overpayment-relief claims; first checks: the GBP 6/week rate and eligibility test per tax year, the four-year claim window (TMA 1970 s43), and that employer reimbursements are netted off (ITEPA 2003 s336/s316A)

evidence.correctness: Ran an independent script (`node /tmp/claude-0/audit-uk-working-from-home-tax-relief-calculator/indep.mjs`) built from GOV.UK homeworking guidance (GBP 6/week from 6 Apr 2020), TMA 1970 s43 and ITEPA 2003 s336. Passes: sample claimable 188 wk x 6 x 20% = 225.6 (observed 225.6); deadline(2022) = 2027-04-05; 52 wk at 40% = 124.8 (matches FAQ 'about GBP 125'); 2021/22 expired as at 2026-11-20; 2025/26 urgent on 2030-01-10. Fails: employer reimbursement is pro-rated by weeks/52, so an employee paid GBP 156 for 26 weeks at home (fully covered) is shown GBP 15.60 relief (expected 0) and GBP 276 for 46 weeks shows GBP 6.37 (expected 0); Scottish rates 41% (2022/23 higher), 46% (2022/23 top) and 47% (2023/24 top) are rejected with 'Pick your income tax rate.' The no-reimbursement path most users take is right; the reimbursement path overstates.
evidence.completeness: `node --test '*.test.mjs'` in the subject root: 27 pass, 0 fail; README's repo-root command also 27/27. Claimed features checked in code and by running compute(): per-year refund (works), deadline per year (works), lost-to-deadline total (works), urgent within 90 days (works), required-by-employer gate zeroes result (works), actual-costs comparison (works), employer payments taken off (works but wrong arithmetic), P87 vs Self Assessment route (works), summary download text (summaryText runs, names VERIFY and 'Not tax advice'). P87_LIMIT is exported but never used, so expenses over GBP 2,500 still get the P87 route. `node platform/pages/served-copy.mjs uk-working-from-home-tax-relief-calculator`: no placeholder or retired origin in what ships.
evidence.verification: Tests 27/27 green. Six seeded mutants with platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: deadline +1 day and urgent window 90->60 were caught; dropping the weeks/52 pro-rating on reimbursement, ignoring reimbursement on actual costs, and computing relief from flat instead of the chosen expenses all SURVIVED, as did act>flat -> act>=flat (near-equivalent, tie label only). Reimbursement and actual-cost relief amounts are not asserted by any test (the reimbursed tests hit the max(0) floor or 52-week cases where pro-rating is a no-op).
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (88 lines), calc.test.mjs, page.test.mjs, usage.mjs, index.html. Pure functions, input rejected with messages rather than clamped, strict date validation, escaped output on the page, local-only imports. Defects: P87_LIMIT dead constant (calc.mjs:12); one annual reimbursement figure applied to every tax year (calc.mjs:31) though payments usually differ by year; minified one-line form markup in index.html. Acceptable for a small static tool.
evidence.claims: Disclaimer, no-warranty and 'Not decided' list present (index.html:101,122; page.test.mjs asserts them). README and page honestly say rules were checked against adviser summaries, not HMRC pages. Unbacked: the finding 'Your employer's payments of GBP 100 a year were taken off' (calc.mjs:73) when run with 10 weeks only took off GBP 19.23 (ran compute with reimbursed 100, weeks 10: 'GBP 8.15 ... on GBP 40.77 of expenses'); FAQ 'Tax-free payments from your employer are taken off first' is likewise not what the code does for part-year home working. 'Not decided: Scottish bands' is stated, but the rate dropdown silently omits year-specific Scottish rates without saying so. llms.txt github.io link is source-only (served copy rewritten).
evidence.fitness: Walked the job for an employee required to work from home 2022/23-2025/26 with no employer payments: enter weeks, pick rate, get per-year refund, deadlines and P87/SA instructions with evidence to keep: complete and correct. Users who received partial employer payments or Scottish taxpayers in 2022/23-2023/24 higher/top bands get a wrong or unavailable answer. Most target users are in the first group, so the job can usually be finished.
evidence.domain: Compared with GOV.UK 'Tax relief for employees: working at home', HMRC EIM32815 (flat-rate GBP 6/week, required-to-work-at-home test from 2022/23), TMA 1970 s43 four-year limit, ITEPA 2003 s336 (only unreimbursed expenses). Rate, eligibility gate, deadline and the end of the relief from 6 April 2026 (Autumn Budget 2025) are right. Departures: reimbursement pro-rated over 52 weeks instead of netted against the claimed weeks' costs; single rate list for all years omits Scottish 41/46/47%; a single marginal rate is used where the extra relief straddles a band boundary (stated limit).

defects.what: Employer reimbursement is pro-rated by weeks/52, so a part-year home worker whose costs the employer fully covered is told they can still claim (GBP 156 for 26 weeks -> GBP 15.60 relief; GBP 276 for 46 weeks -> GBP 6.37). ITEPA s336 allows relief only on unreimbursed costs; the user would file a claim HMRC should refuse.
Finding text says the employer's whole annual payment 'was taken off' while the code deducted only weeks/52 of it (GBP 100 entered, GBP 19.23 deducted); FAQ repeats the claim.
One rate list for every year omits Scottish 41% and 46% (2022/23) and 47% (2023/24); those taxpayers cannot get a result for those years and are not told why.
Reimbursement, actual-cost relief and the chosen-expenses relief amount are untested: three seeded mutants in that arithmetic survived.
P87_LIMIT (GBP 2,500) is defined but never used, so actual-cost claims above it are still sent to form P87 rather than Self Assessment.
A single annual reimbursement figure is subtracted in every tax year, though payments typically differ by year (or stop).
llms.txt links the old github.io address; the deploy rewrites it (served copy clean).

verdict: A small, honest tool whose main path is right: for an employee required to work from home with no employer payments, the GBP 6/week x marginal-rate refund, the four-year deadline per tax year and the expired 2021/22 window all recompute exactly against GOV.UK guidance and TMA 1970 s43 (5 of 5 such checks pass). It misses the bar on correctness, claims, verification and domain because employer reimbursement is pro-rated over 52 weeks (a fully reimbursed part-year worker is shown a refund), the finding text overstates what was deducted, Scottish 2022/23-2023/24 higher/top rates cannot be selected, and the tests miss the reimbursement and actual-cost arithmetic (4 of 6 mutants survived).
